rationale: iter-15: shrink learnable residual-scale alpha init from 0.1 to 0.05 (single-knob change vs iter-14 kept). Hypothesis: even gentler near-identity start composes better with zero-init tail. Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6474 (-2.4%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5585 (-4.9%). Strong regression. Interpretation: at lr=1e-4 for only 8 epochs, alpha=0.05 is too small to lift the residual signal — the network spends training budget growing alpha from 0.05 rather than refining the conv kernels, and never catches up. alpha=0.1 from iter-14 is near the sweet spot for this schedule. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: EDSR residual-scale alpha is sensitive to training-budget interaction: smaller init means more epochs needed to grow alpha. With fixed 8-epoch budget, alpha=0.1 beats alpha=0.05 substantially. Test larger alpha (0.2) before assuming 0.1 is optimal — or test zero-init alpha (ReZero) only if also raising epochs / lr.
